raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this season.

I've got my 5 mu and it's wheat-maize like always. Five mu isn't much — my wife and I both pick up work in town when we can, and honestly the field is more about keeping our own grain in the bin than getting rich. Still, I've been doing this 10 years and I know what works on my plot.

**Wheat (already in the ground from October):** I planted Jimai variety mid-October like everyone around here. Put down about 20 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before planting — that's my base. Now in spring at jointing I'll topdress urea, maybe 15 kg/mu. Extension guy at the township station last year said 14 kg N total is enough but I usually push it a bit more, around 17-18 kg N/mu total, because last year my neighbor cut back and his wheat looked thin. I'd rather spend the extra 30 yuan than lose 50 kg of grain. Should get around 450 kg/mu if the spring rains come, maybe 480 if I'm lucky. Will irrigate 3 times — green-up, jointing, and grain-fill. Pumping costs are the killer, about 25 yuan/mu each time.

**Maize (going in mid-June):** Right after wheat harvest, no time to waste. I'll do no-till direct seeding with the village's hired planter — 30 yuan/mu and saves me 3 days. Zhengdan 958 seed, what most folks use here. Apply about 25 kg compound at planting, then topdress 15 kg urea at the big-flare stage when the plant's about knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water if the summer rains cooperate — I'll irrigate once or twice depending on July weather. Spray once for armyworm, that's been bad the last two years. Expect around 500 kg/mu.

**My main worry:** Urea price. It went up last year and the news says it might go up again. If it does I'll cut my topdress a little, maybe drop to 12 kg. Five mu doesn't give me much room.
